findings.issue: AC#2 always builds views with the default empty earlierShowdowns, so the property run never carries a non-empty list through actWith.
findings.evidence: playerView(state, seat) and actWith(state, ...) are called without a third argument. The spec allows this (section 7: 'SPEC-02 (empty)'), and SPEC-01 covers the non-empty pass-through.
findings.fix: Optional: pass a fixed earlierShowdowns list (e.g. showdownOf of a pre-played hand) to both playerView calls and actWith. Not required by the spec.

summary: player-view.ts matches the section 5 design. It copies every field by name: the viewer's own hole cards, fresh copies of stakes, board, pots and eligible lists, actions and players (8 named fields, no holeCards), and legalActions only for toAct. earlierShowdowns is passed through by reference (A-3). There is no deck, burned or result field and no shared mutable object. actWith returns hand-complete without calling the policy, and showdownOf follows result.showdown order. The SPEC-08 grep prints nothing, and the gate (fix-2) passed lint, typecheck, tests and the 619/620-line budget. I ran the player-view tests on a scratch copy of the repo against 14 mutants of player-view.ts, and every one was caught: (1) spreading ...p into players, (2) adding burned, (3) adding deck, (4) another seat's hole card in holeCards, (5) actions by reference, (6) holeCards by reference, (7) eligible by reference, (8) copying earlierShowdowns, (9) legalActions for every seat, (10) plain Error instead of RangeError, (11) showdownOf on fold-outs, (12) actWith building seat 1's view, (13) removing the hand-complete short-circuit, (14) widening SeatPolicy to PlayerView | HandState. Mutants 1, 2, 3, 4 and 12 also fail the AC#2 property test, so it can genuinely fail. That test is self-checking too: every hidden index must change and every visible index must stay, the own-card swap control must make the views differ, and it runs at every decision point of 300 hands with 3-10 seats. The AC#3 probe checks the exact TS2345 lines [6, 7] in probe.ts and the text 'PlayerView', and its control probe must exit 0. Nothing the spec requires was dropped by the assertion trimming. One NIT; no BLOCKER or MAJOR.
